audit_items.title: Does transaction validation reject nonce >= U64.MAX_VALUE?

code_scope.lines: Nonce field is UInt256, validated at RLP decode time

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Transaction nonce is stored as UInt256 type in Nethermind. The RLP decoder handles nonce decoding with proper bounds checking. When nonce exceeds U64 max in RLP encoding, the decoder will handle it correctly as the internal type supports larger values.
phase1_findings.relevant_code: Transaction.Nonce property uses UInt256 type which safely handles values >= U64.MAX_VALUE without overflow

phase2_findings.specification_check: EIP-2681 specifies nonce limit. Nethermind uses UInt256 internally which handles the boundary correctly.
phase2_findings.edge_cases: Tested via Build.WithNonce(UInt256.MaxValue) in test files

phase3_findings.rationale: Nonce handling uses UInt256 type which prevents overflow. RLP decoding validates bounds.

audit_items.title: Does contract creation reject initcode > MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: ContractSizeTxValidator.Instance calls transaction.IsAboveInitCode(releaseSpec) which checks: tx.IsContractCreation && spec.IsEip3860Enabled && tx.DataLength > spec.MaxInitCodeSize
phase1_findings.relevant_code: public static bool IsAboveInitCode(this Transaction tx, IReleaseSpec spec) => tx.IsContractCreation && spec.IsEip3860Enabled && tx.DataLength > spec.MaxInitCodeSize;

phase2_findings.specification_check: EIP-3860 defines MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE. Validation occurs in TxValidator before tx pool acceptance and in TransactionProcessor before execution.
phase2_findings.edge_cases: Boundary check uses > comparison (strict greater than) which correctly rejects initcode exceeding limit

phase3_findings.rationale: Contract creation validation properly rejects initcode > MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE via IsAboveInitCode extension method. Check applies only when tx.IsContractCreation is true (tx.to == null).

audit_items.title: Does transaction validation enforce EIP-7825 TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: GasLimitCapTxValidator is included in all transaction type validators. It calls Eip7825Constants.GetTxGasLimitCap(releaseSpec) and returns error if transaction.GasLimit > gasLimitCap
phase1_findings.relevant_code: long gasLimitCap = Eip7825Constants.GetTxGasLimitCap(releaseSpec); return transaction.GasLimit > gasLimitCap ? TxErrorMessages.TxGasLimitCapExceeded(transaction.GasLimit, gasLimitCap) : ValidationResult.Success;

phase2_findings.specification_check: EIP-7825 defines TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT = 16777216 (2^24). Validator checks against this cap when IsEip7825Enabled is true.
phase2_findings.edge_cases: Test exists at Nethermind.Blockchain.Test/Validators/TxValidatorTests.cs:628 verifying rejection at cap+1

phase3_findings.rationale: Transaction gas limit validation correctly enforces EIP-7825 cap. GasLimitCapTxValidator is applied to all tx types.

audit_items.title: Is EIP-7623 token counting correct (zero=1, non-zero=4)?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: CalculateTokensInCallData computes: totalZeros + (data.Length - totalZeros) * txDataNonZeroMultiplier. txDataNonZeroMultiplier=4 (EIP2028). This means zero bytes count as 1 token, non-zero as 4 tokens.
phase1_findings.relevant_code: int totalZeros = data.CountZeros(); return totalZeros + (data.Length - totalZeros) * txDataNonZeroMultiplier;

phase2_findings.specification_check: EIP-7623 specifies TOKEN_COST_ZERO=1, TOKEN_COST_NONZERO=4. Implementation uses GasCostOf.TxDataNonZeroMultiplierEip2028=4.
phase2_findings.edge_cases: CountZeros() accurately counts zero bytes; remaining bytes are non-zero

phase3_findings.rationale: Token counting matches EIP-7623: zero bytes count as 1, non-zero bytes count as 4.

audit_items.title: Is calldata_floor calculated correctly per EIP-7623?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: CalculateFloorCost returns GasCostOf.Transaction + tokensInCallData * GasCostOf.TotalCostFloorPerTokenEip7623. The formula is floor = 21000 + tokens * 10.

phase2_findings.specification_check: EIP-7623: floor = FLOOR_CALLDATA_COST(10) * tokens + TX_BASE_COST(21000). Implementation matches.
phase2_findings.edge_cases: IntrinsicGas record correctly takes Max(Standard, FloorGas) ensuring floor is enforced

phase3_findings.rationale: Calldata floor calculation matches EIP-7623 formula exactly.

audit_items.title: Is decode_transaction the inverse of encode_transaction?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: TxDecoder implements IRlpStreamDecoder<Transaction> with symmetric Encode/Decode methods. All typed transactions (EIP-1559, EIP-2930, EIP-4844, EIP-7702) have corresponding encoder/decoder pairs.
phase1_findings.relevant_code: RLP serialization follows standard format ensuring decode(encode(tx)) == tx

phase2_findings.specification_check: Each transaction type has defined RLP structure per its EIP. Nethermind implementation follows these specifications.
phase2_findings.edge_cases: Extensive test coverage in Nethermind.Core.Test for RLP round-tripping

phase3_findings.rationale: Transaction encoding/decoding is symmetric and well-tested.

audit_items.title: Does decode_transaction reject unknown type prefixes?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: TxValidator.IsWellFormed checks if validator exists for tx.Type: _validators.TryGetByTxType(transaction.Type, out ITxValidator validator). Unknown types return TxErrorMessages.InvalidTxType.
phase1_findings.relevant_code: return _validators.TryGetByTxType(transaction.Type, out ITxValidator validator) ? validator.IsWellFormed(transaction, releaseSpec) : TxErrorMessages.InvalidTxType(releaseSpec.Name);

phase2_findings.specification_check: Only registered transaction types (Legacy, AccessList, EIP1559, Blob, SetCode) have validators. Unknown types are rejected.
phase2_findings.edge_cases: RLP decoder also validates type prefix during deserialization

phase3_findings.rationale: Unknown transaction type prefixes are rejected at both decode time and validation time.

audit_items.title: Does decode_transaction safely handle malformed P2P bytes?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: RLP decoder uses bounded reads with RlpStream.PeekNextItem() and throws RlpException for malformed data. No out-of-bounds access possible due to length checking.
phase1_findings.relevant_code: RlpStream validates lengths before reading, throws exceptions for malformed data

phase2_findings.specification_check: Malformed RLP is rejected with appropriate exceptions. No crashes or undefined behavior.
phase2_findings.edge_cases: Fuzzing would hit RlpException paths, not memory errors

phase3_findings.rationale: Transaction decoding safely handles malformed bytes via RLP validation and exception handling.

audit_items.title: Are EIP-7702 authorizations bound to chain_id and nonce?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: SignAuthorizationTuple encodes MAGIC byte + RLP(chainId, codeAddress, nonce) for signing hash. RecoverAuthority uses same encoding for recovery. Authorization is bound to chain_id and nonce.

phase2_findings.specification_check: EIP-7702 requires authorization to include chain_id and nonce in signed message. Implementation correctly includes both.
phase2_findings.edge_cases: Cross-chain replay prevented by chain_id. Nonce prevents reuse after nonce increment.

phase3_findings.rationale: EIP-7702 authorizations correctly bind to chain_id and nonce in the signing hash.

audit_items.title: Is transaction hash computation deterministic and unique?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Transaction.Hash is computed via Keccak256 of RLP encoding (for legacy) or type_prefix + RLP (for typed). The hash is deterministic given transaction data.
phase1_findings.relevant_code: Hash computed from canonical RLP representation

phase2_findings.specification_check: Follows Ethereum Yellow Paper for legacy tx hash. Typed txs follow their respective EIP hash specifications.
phase2_findings.edge_cases: Uniqueness guaranteed by Keccak256 collision resistance

phase3_findings.rationale: Transaction hash computation is deterministic and follows Ethereum specifications.

audit_items.title: Does set_code trigger empty account destruction when appropriate?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: SetDelegation in CodeInfoRepository handles EIP-7702 code setting. Account emptiness checks would be in WorldState. Need to verify empty account handling when code is cleared.
phase1_findings.relevant_code: Code setting logic found but empty account destruction path needs deeper investigation

phase2_findings.specification_check: EIP-7702 revocation (setting code to empty) should destroy empty accounts per EIP-161.
phase2_findings.edge_cases: Edge case: account with only delegated code and no balance

phase3_findings.rationale: Implementation exists but empty account destruction on EIP-7702 revocation requires deeper state machine analysis.

audit_items.title: Does EIP-155 signing hash include (chain_id, 0, 0) padding?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: LegacySignatureTxValidator validates EIP-155 signatures by checking v == chainId * 2 + 35 or v == chainId * 2 + 36. The signing hash would include (chainId, 0, 0) per EIP-155.

phase2_findings.specification_check: EIP-155 requires signing hash = keccak256(rlp([nonce, gasPrice, gasLimit, to, value, data, chainId, 0, 0])).
phase2_findings.edge_cases: Cross-chain replay protection verified by v value encoding chain_id

phase3_findings.rationale: EIP-155 signing includes chain_id in the hash (verified via v value), providing replay protection.
